IN MFA NO.6157/2016 IS FILED UNDER ORDER 41 RULE 22 OF CPC., AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 27.5.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.121/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, MADIKERI,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
THIS MFA AND MFA CROB.

, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In these appeals, both Insurance Company (6th respondent) as well as the petitioner have challenged the judgment and award dated 27.05.2016 in M.V.C.No.121/2013 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Madikeri ('the Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.07.2012 at about 05:45 pm, the petitioner while travelling in the car bearing Reg.No.KA-12/P-3222 with co-passenger Smt. Geetha Narendra from Kushalnagar on NC: 2023:KHC:41352 Madikeri-Kushalnagar road near Basavanahalli Village, from the opposite direction a jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-34/M-1243 hit against their car, injuring the petitioner.
After taking treatment at Vivus Hospital, Madikeri, she approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Companies of the car as well as the jeep.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.1,66,987/- with 9% interest p.a. fastening the liability against respondents No.1 to 6 and directed respondent No.6 to deposit the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, respondent No.6/Insurance Company has filed this appeal and seeking enhancement, the petitioner has filed the cross-objection.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. B.C. Seetharama Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.6/Insurace Company, Sri. N. Jagadish NC: 2023:KHC:41352 Baliga, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.
Geetha Raj, learned Counsel for the 4th respondent/National Insurance Company Ltd.
5.
It is the contention of learned counsel for the respondent No.6/Insurance Company that there is no negligence on part of the jeep, the driver of the car was charge sheeted.
The petitioner is the inmate of the car, on behalf of the petitioner, no independent evidence is let-in to prove the accident.

On behalf of the Insurance Company, the driver of the jeep is examined and the Tribunal United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt. S S Syla Shankar on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95989168/
4 has not evaluated the spot sketch as well as the Mahazar which clearly explains complete negligence on the part of the driver of the car; joint liability fastened against the jeep is erroneous,
compensation assessed is on the higher side so also the interest of 9% is disproportionate and he sought for interference.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner was aged 64 years,
she being the car passenger, sustained fracture of both the bones of right leg; at this age, she has suffered more than 50% disability, spent huge money towards treatment; but the Tribunal did not consider the seriousness of the injuries, disability, loss of amenities and discomfort suffered by the petitioner and he sought for enhancement.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. It is the specific case of the Insurance Company of the jeep that the complete negligence is on part of the car, the contribution by the jeep is 'zero' in resulting the accident.
Jeep was on its left side, the car has gone to its right side while hitting against the jeep.

The Tribunal though referred these aspects, only on the ground that the petitioner is NC: 2023:KHC:41352 claiming compensation against both the Insurance Companies, 6th respondent was directed to deposit the compensation.
9. The petitioner is also an eye witness to the accident, she claims that it is the jeep which came and hit against the car.
Quite natural, petitioner is the passenger of the car.
Her cross-examination demonstrated that she could not able to explain how the accident took place.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar drawn at the time of investigation.
On careful perusal of the sketch prepared and the mahazar, it is pertinent to note that the place of accident is Madikeri-Kushalnagar Main Road having a width of 7 meters.

The jeep was on the complete left side of the road towards Kushalnagar,
whereas the car had gone off to the mid-line of the road, traversed to the right side of the road instead of going towards left side i.e., towards Madikeri.
This clearly points out that if the car had traversed on its left side, there is NC: 2023:KHC:41352 no accident.

Hence, it is the car which has gone to the off-side while hitting against the jeep and for this reason, the criminal prosecution was initiated against respondent No.1 who is the driver of the car and he has been charge sheeted after the investigation.
10.
The finding recorded by the Tribunal that there is negligence on part of the driver of the jeep is not proper.
The jeep and its Insurance Company is arrayed as parties, because of involvement of two vehicles, the Tribunal cannot attribute complete negligence on part of the jeep.
Hence, the finding recorded by the Tribunal is contrary to the material on record.
Hence, the jeep has to be exonerated from any negligence, particularly the aspect of contributory negligence and the petitioner has to claim the compensation from the owner and insurer of the car.
11. Medical records point out that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both the bones and right leg.

sentences.text: Dr. Kumar has stated on oath that the petitioner was treated under hospitalization at Vivus Hospital and it is he who treated her as an Orthopedic Surgeon, he has given an opinion that the petitioner has suffered 15% whole body disability.
Therefore, the assessment of disability is proper.
The accident took place in the year 2012, the petitioner claims that she was earning Rs.10,000/- per month by doing agriculture.
She has not produced any proof of income.
Hence, she has to be treated as a person with no proof of income.

In the year 2012, a person with no proof of income has to be assessed not less than Rs.7,000/- instead of Rs.3,000/- assessed by the Tribunal and accordingly, the income of the petitioner has to be assessed.

For the age of 65,
applicable multiplier is '7' and accordingly, loss of future earnings has to be calculated.
Then, loss of future earnings will be Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 7 x 15% = Rs.88,200/-.

Considering the nature of injuries,
hospitalization - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41352 and the treatment, the compensation has to be assessed as follows:
Sl. No. Particulars

Rs . 
 1 Pain and sufferings 20,000  2 Medical expenses 1,03,287  3 Loss of amenities and discomfort 20,000  4 Loss of income during laid-up for 3 21,000  months (Rs.7,000/- x 3)
 5
Attendant charges, food and 15,000  nourishment and travelling  expenses  6 Loss of future earnings 88,200
11.1. Total compensation comes to Rs.2,67,487/- as against Rs.1,66,987/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,00,500/- rounded off to Rs.1,00,000/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
12. Adverting to the rate of interest is concerned, no doubt that in the year 2016, no banks were offering interest at 9% p.a. on any fixed deposit.
As regarding the rate of interest is - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41352 concerned, it is noticed that there are variations from one judgment to another, there is no uniformity.

In this regard, the Division Bench of this Court in Ms. Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -Vs- Venkateshan. V and Ors.1 in with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt. S S Syla Shankar on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95989168/

sentences.text:
Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest, it reads thus:
"52.Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.
In view of the above settled principles, the rate of interest has to be maintained uniformly at 6% and accordingly the petitioner is entitled to interest.

As regarding liability is concerned, since there is no contributory negligence on part of the jeep,
no liability can be fastened against it.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the driver, respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.3 being the insurer of car are jointly liable to pay the compensation and the liability against the jeep is exonerated.
Accordingly, both the appeals merit consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Both the appeal and cross-objection are allowed-in-part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.
iii) The petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,67,487/- with 6% interest p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondent No.3/Insurance Company of the car is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41352 the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
is exonerated.

vi) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
